key_insight: A mid-level QISA for local logical operations best balances scalability and control complexity for fault-tolerant quantum computing on cryogenic fixed-connectivity hardware.
engineering_relevance: For superconducting and topological quantum processors, choosing too-low or too-high instruction abstractions can either break thermal budgets or overload the control stack, directly shaping classical-quantum co-design.
method: Introduced the ARIES instruction-set hierarchy to compare QISA abstraction levels.
Built an end-to-end, cycle-accurate toolflow with a classical driver and hardware-engine simulator.
Evaluated eight quantum applications on superconducting and topological qubit platforms.
evidence_signal: The study measured instruction bandwidth, transceiver power dissipation, and measurement-processing overheads, showing physical-level QISAs exceed dilution-refrigerator thermal limits while canonical-level QISAs underestimate routing congestion and runtime.
watch_item: Results depend on the assumed cryogenic fixed-connectivity platforms and the fidelity of the simulator/modeling assumptions, so hardware-specific validation is still needed.
paper_title: Architecting Instruction Execution for Scalable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
